content.title: Sixers vs. Nets: Game Preview, Injury Report and How to Watch | Mar. 14, 2026
content.text: With his fourth 3-pointer of the game – and of the first quarter – on Thursday, Feb. 26, 2026 against the Miami Heat at Xfinity Mobile Arena, Tyrese Maxey became the Philadelphia 76ers’ franchise leader for 3-pointers made with 886. The sixth-year guard surpassed Allen Iverson, who made 885 threes in 722 games with the Sixers. It took 375 games for Maxey, who finished Thursday’s win with five threes for 887 overall.“Once I heard about [the approaching milestone], I definitely wanted to do it at the crib,” Maxey said postgame. “I think the fans are a big part of my success. I’m very thankful to all the fans. Philadelphia, we have a special connection.“And to wear these [Iverson-era black] jerseys, that’s fun. A.I. is somebody we’ve all looked up to – someone I’ve looked up to being a small guard. To be able to pass him in anything in basketball, that’s cool. To have my name next to his, it’s a blessing.”Most importantly, the Sixers defeated the Heat 124-117. Maxey recorded a team-high 28 points and game highs of 11 assists and five steals.In his lone college season at the University of Kentucky, the eventual 2020 No. 21 overall pick shot 29.2% from beyond the arc. In a relatively small sample size of 113 3-point attempts – about four per game – Maxey made 33.It took the now two-time NBA All-Star six professional games to connect on his first career 3-pointer, a right-wing shot on Jan. 2, 2021, against Charlotte.Two seasons later – on Oct. 28, 2022, in Toronto – Maxey made a career-high nine threes, tying the single-game franchise record held by Dana Barros and Danny Green. Paul George matched the mark on Jan. 27, 2026, against Milwaukee.Now, Maxey is one of the league’s top shooters.After the Miami game, Maxey is tied for second in the league with 191 threes. He competed in his first NBA 3-Point Contest at 2026 All-Star Weekend in Los Angeles.“I know I can shoot the ball well,” Maxey said when asked if the 3-Point Contest was gratifying, considering there were some early skeptics.“I know I’m able to shoot threes.”The Sixers’ top 10 list now reads: Maxey, Iverson, Robert Covington, Kyle Korver, Tobias Harris, Joel Embiid, Andre Iguodala, Hersey Hawkins, JJ Redick and Furkan Korkmaz.“[Maxey] has a unique kind of double threat, which is the speed and the really deep shooting range,” 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said after Maxey’s career-high 54 points at Milwaukee in November. “He's just really talented. His confidence continues to grow, and his teammates' confidence in him continues to grow.”
